title: The Far Current
premise: Petra Coldharbour, a riverboat captain who has spent a lifetime staying invisible on the Vell, runs salvage for people who'd rather not be named. When an unprecedented low tide exposes a sea cave said to hold the drowned treasury of a deposed dynasty, she salvages one artifact to pay off the debt that could take her boat—and finds herself hunted by the Consortium agent who financed her loan and by the stranger, Emeric Vale, who claims to be the dynasty's last heir. Trapped together through the monsoon with a holed hull and rising water, Petra must choose between selling Emeric out to buy her freedom or running the flooded gorge at monsoon peak. She runs it, loses the boat, and surfaces with proof of the heir's identity—choosing, for the first time, to be seen.
about_author: Ivo Crane is the pen name of a former barge pilot who spent eleven years working inland waterways before turning to fiction. Their novels are known for river-true detail and protagonists who would rather outrun their pasts than explain them.

chapters.title: The Mood of Sandbars
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. A routine night salvage run up the Vell establishes her world: the leaky ketch Marrow, her mounting debt to the Consortium, and her talent for reading water no chart records. She refuses a passenger at the dock—a man in city clothes watching her too closely. Beat: competence as armor; loneliness disguised as independence.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gives Back
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. An unheard-of spring low tide drains the cliffs below Gullwatch Point, exposing a cave mouth locals call the King's Purse. Petra explores far enough to confirm legends of the drowned dynasty's treasury, then retreats—but not before pocketing a signet ring to pawn. Beat: temptation dressed as pragmatism.

chapters.title: The Pawnbroker's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. In Saltmouth, the pawnbroker recognizes the ring and goes pale; word spreads faster than Petra can leave port. The Consortium's collector, Dame Sable Quist, appears at the dock holding Petra's loan papers and makes an offer: find what else the tide revealed, or lose the Marrow. Beat: the trap closing quietly.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Rail
chapters.summary: Emeric's POV. The man from the dock—Emeric Vale—buys passage under a false name, then admits he knows who she is and what she took. He claims to be the last heir of the drowned line and says the ring is his by blood. He offers her triple Quist's price to carry him to the cave. Beat: distrust sharpened by need.

chapters.title: Two Debts, One Boat
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra weighs Quist against Emeric and chooses neither: she'll reach the cave first on her own terms. But the Marrow's old planking is weeping worse than usual, and the barometer begins its long fall toward monsoon. She signs on Emeric as deckhand instead of passenger—her rules, her boat. Beat: control asserted, already fraying.

chapters.title: The King's Purse
chapters.summary: Dual POV. They dive the cave at slack water: coins fused into coral, a sealed lead chest bearing the royal cipher. Emeric opens the chest with a story only an heir could know—and inside is a ledger naming every family the dynasty betrayed, including the Coldharbours. Beat: wonder curdling into history's long grudge.

chapters.title: Ledger of the Drowned
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The ledger shows Petra's own great-grandfather sold the fleet's loyalty cheap and was paid in silence. Emeric argues the treasure belongs to the dispossessed; Petra argues nothing that deep stays buried without reason. Quist's launch appears on the horizon. Beat: the past stops being abstract.

chapters.title: Running Before the Weather
chapters.summary: Emeric's POV. They flee downriver ahead of Quist as the monsoon's first bands hit—squalls, zero visibility, the Marrow laboring. Emeric proves unexpectedly able in a blow and asks about the scar on Petra's hand; she gives him half the truth. Beat: reluctant partnership forming under pressure.

chapters.title: Quist's Terms
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Quist corners them at a fueling lock and offers Petra full debt forgiveness for Emeric alone—the heir, delivered. Petra stalls, and Quist lets her, certain survival will do the negotiating. That night Petra catches Emeric trying to copy the ledger pages. Beat: betrayal suspected from both directions.

chapters.title: The Hole Below the Waterline
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Grounding on an uncharted snag opens the Marrow's seams. They beach her in a mangrove creek, bilge running around the clock, monsoon proper arriving overhead. Stripped to survival, they trade stories: Emeric's childhood exile, Petra's father lost running the gorge. Beat: intimacy born of shared danger.

chapters.title: What Survival Costs
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Repairs demand trading the salvaged coins to a creek-side scrap dealer—spending the treasure to save the boat that carries it. Petra realizes she's been paying for her invisibility her whole life and it never once held. Emeric proposes the gorge run: only the flooded gorge can lose Quist. Beat: resolve hardening into decision.

chapters.title: The Creek at High Water
chapters.summary: Emeric's POV. Quist's men find the creek. A night skirmish among the mangroves; Petra takes a gash, Emeric takes a beating protecting the ledger. They escape downstream but the Marrow's patch is failing and the gorge window—two days of peak flood—is closing. Beat: the cost made physical.

chapters.title: Charts Drawn in Fear
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra plans the run from memory of her father's fatal attempt, drawing the channel from a child's recollection. Emeric questions whether the treasure justifies dying for it; Petra answers that it was never about the treasure—it's about not being owned. Beat: motive clarified; fear acknowledged.

chapters.title: The Last Safe Harbor
chapters.summary: Dual POV. They shelter at a derelict light station where Emeric reveals the full truth: he isn't after restoration—he means to publish the ledger and dissolve the Consortium's founding claim, which traces to the same stolen treasury. Quist isn't collecting for money; she's erasing evidence. Beat: stakes transformed from personal to historical.

chapters.title: Quist Closes In
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Quist offers a final bargain at the station door: the Marrow, the debt, and Petra's clean record—for the ledger and the heir. She leaves a deadline: dawn. Petra spends the night repairing the patch by lamplight while Emeric sleeps, deciding alone. Beat: the loneliest hour; choice crystallizing.

chapters.title: Dawn Bargain
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. At dawn Petra tells Quist yes—then uses the meeting to stall while Emeric warms the engine. When Quist realizes, her men open fire; the Marrow casts off under fire, patch straining, heading straight for the gorge mouth as the flood peaks. Beat: commitment irreversible.

chapters.title: The Far Current
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The gorge run: Petra steering by her father's remembered channel through standing waves and collapsed rockfall, Emeric on the bilge pump, the Marrow coming apart around them. They thread the far current—the deep channel her father died seeking—and shoot out the other side as the boat founders in calmer water. Beat: climax; grief and triumph in one breath.

chapters.title: Wreckage and Witnesses
chapters.summary: Emeric's POV. They swim ashore among fishing families who watched the whole run—witnesses Quist cannot disappear. The ledger, waterproofed in the lead chest, survives. Quist's launch, forced back by the gorge, is seen turning away. Beat: safety found not in hiding but in being seen by many eyes.

chapters.title: The Reading at Saltmouth
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Emeric publishes the ledger publicly at the Saltmouth fish market; the Consortium's charter claim collapses under its own documented theft. Quist departs rather than face inquiry. Petra expects nothing for herself and is named anyway—as witness, as captain, as Coldharbour. Beat: identity claimed, not conferred.

chapters.title: Salvage Rights
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Salvors raise the Marrow; Petra decides to rebuild her rather than replace her, financing it with the last of the recovered coins—debt repaid on her own terms. Emeric offers her partnership in something larger; she declines for now, but doesn't close the door. Beat: quiet aftermath; agency retained.

chapters.title: High Water Mark
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Weeks later, Petra pilots the rebuilt Marrow past Gullwatch Point at ordinary tide—the cave sealed again beneath the sea. She visits her father's grave and tells him about the far current. For the first time she takes on a paying passenger without checking who's asking. Beat: peace earned, vigilance kept.

chapters.title: Every Sandbar's Mood
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, coda. A letter arrives from Emeric: the restitution hearings begin, and her testimony is wanted. Petra reads it at the rail, looks at the water she knows better than any chart, and turns the Marrow toward Saltmouth—not fleeing this time, but arriving. Beat: the invisible woman, visible at last, choosing the current forward.
